papers.title_en: Humanoid SRL: Augmenting Humanoids with Supernumerary Limbs for Coordinated Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Fukang Liu, Feiyang Wu, Paul Barsa, Jaehwi Jang, Akshat Jain, Zhigen Zhao, Yipu Chen, Zhaoyuan Gu, Nikhil Vemuri, Anshul Chandaliya, Kaijie Zhu, Sean Lublinsky, Matthew Zhu, Tony G. Chen, Ye Zhao
papers.evidence: 通过超限肢体实现人形机器人全身协调与平衡
papers.tldr: 人形机器人双臂被占用或需额外接触时，其拟人形态会限制全身移动操作。本文为人形平台集成超数机械臂，用基于模型的轨迹优化为目标条件强化学习生成动态可行运动，并实现仿真到硬件的零样本迁移。两套配置的分析与实验表明，新增肢体扩展了全身交互能力，可协调操作与支撑，完成接触丰富的三臂移动操作。作者还用硬件示范训练的扩散策略展示视觉引导自主执行，说明人形形态可作为可扩展的机器人增强设计空间。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid robots are envisioned to perform diverse human-level tasks through their anthropomorphic morphology. Their dual-arm configuration enables a broad range of everyday actions. Yet, as in humans, this morphology can constrain loco-manipulation when both arms are occupied or additional contacts are required beyond their reach. Supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) offer a way to extend these capabilities, but their integration requires the added limb to be coordinated with whole-body motion and balance. In this study, we develop and integrate a supernumerary arm into a humanoid platform to investigate how morphological augmentation reshapes its feasible action space. Through quantitative analysis and hardware experiments across two configurations, we show how the additional limb expands whole-body interaction capabilities by enabling manipulation and support to be coordinated beyond the constraints of the native dual-arm configuration. To control this augmented morphology, we leverage model-based trajectory optimization (TO) to generate dynamically feasible motions for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (RL) controllers. The controllers are trained in simulation and transferred to hardware in a zero-shot manner, enabling coordinated whole-body skills for contact-rich tri-arm loco-manipulation. We further show vision-guided autonomous execution on selected tasks using diffusion policies trained from hardware demonstrations. Our findings suggest that humanoid morphology need not be restricted to human-like forms, but can be reimagined as an extensible design space for robotic augmentation.

papers.title_en: Fast Motion Retargeting Pipeline for Scalable Humanoid Robot Learning
papers.authors: Daniel Marew, Sangjun Park, Nisal Perera, Donghyun Kim
papers.evidence: 支撑人形模仿学习的快速运动重定向流水线
papers.tldr: 将大规模人体动捕数据重定向到不同人形机器人仍受限于计算昂贵和逐动作手动调参。FRDV 先用带机器人约束的快速运动学重定向，结合自定义 SQP、Real-Time Iteration 与并行分块处理，再用 contact implicit iLQR 做全刚体动力学验证。其运动学阶段可达 9156 帧/秒，比 GMR 和 ProtoMotions 快约 136 倍，并能识别动力学不可行动作、缓解地面穿透、自碰撞、脚漂浮与脚滑。该流程提升重定向可扩展性，并在 Unitree G1 上完成 sim-to-real 验证，为人形机器人学习提供高效数据管线。
papers.abstract_en: While large-scale human motion capture datasets provide a rich source of demonstrations for humanoid robot learning, retargeting the diverse motions to different humanoid robots remains a nontrivial challenge. Existing kinodynamic trajectory optimization pipelines are computationally expensive and often require manual adjustments per motion. We present FRDV (Fast Retargeting with Dynamics Validation), a scalable framework consisting of rapid constrained kinematic retargeting and an additional dynamics validation pipeline. Its kinematic stage integrates a custom Sequential Quadratic Programming solver, Real-Time Iteration, and parallel chunk-based processing, achieving up to 9,156 frames per second, approximately up to 136 times faster than GMR and ProtoMotions, while robot-specific constraints are incorporated into the optimization to reduce common retargeting artifacts, such as ground penetration and self-collision. For motions requiring additional verification, a contact implicit iLQR controller is utilized to test the retargeted reference under full rigid body dynamics. This dynamics-based validation identifies dynamically infeasible motions and refines contact-related artifacts such as foot floating and foot skating. We evaluate retargeting quality by training motion tracking reinforcement learning policies using several state-of-the-art pipelines and comparing their tracking fidelity and success rates. Furthermore, sim-to-real transfer is demonstrated on a Unitree G1 humanoid. Videos and code are available at: https://daroslab.github.io/frdv/.

papers.title_en: PolyMorph: Learning Locomotion Policy for Cross-Embodiment Adaptation
papers.authors: Hyunsik Oh, Seunghun Jeon, Donghoon Youm, Jungwoo Hur, Hyeongjun Kim, Jeong Hyun Lee, Moonkyu Jung, Jemin Hwangbo
papers.evidence: 面向多形态腿足机器人的形态条件强化学习运动策略
papers.tldr: 腿足机器人强化学习运动策略通常绑定单一形态，腿数、关节或机械参数变化便需重新训练。PolyMorph 将 URDF 拆成关节-连杆模块，结合循环编码器、图 Transformer 与逐关节解码器，学习形态条件化的统一运动策略。训练中引入形态归一化奖励、自适应机器人采样和 URDF 派生 PD 增益初始化以提升稳定性。仿真覆盖双足、三足、四足及未见形态变体，并在多配置真实四足平台部署；单一策略无需逐机器人重训即可跨形态泛化。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning has enabled robust locomotion for legged robots, but learned policies are typically tied to a specific robot morphology and require additional engineering when the number of legs, actuators, or mechanical properties change. We present PolyMorph, a morphology-conditioned framework that learns a single locomotion policy for heterogeneous legged robots. PolyMorph converts each robot's URDF into joint-link modules and combines a recurrent encoder, graph-based Transformer, and per-joint decoder to generate actions across variable leg counts and joint configurations. To improve training stability, PolyMorph uses morphology-normalized rewards, adaptive robot sampling, and URDF-derived PD-gain initialization. We evaluate PolyMorph in simulation across bipedal, tripedal, and quadrupedal robots, including unseen morphology variants and platforms, and deploy the policy on real quadruped platforms operated in multiple configurations. The results show that a single PolyMorph policy generalizes across diverse robot morphologies without per-robot policy retraining.

papers.title_en: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation For Robot Policies
papers.authors: Motasem Alfarra, Pietro Mazzaglia, Markus Peschl, Daniel Dijkman, Christos Louizos
papers.evidence: 在地形与负载变化下对强化学习运动策略进行测试时自适应
papers.tldr: 机器人策略在部署时遇到地形、负载或传感变化容易失效，而重训练和人工校准受设备时延与内存限制。论文研究无奖励、自监督的测试时适应，以冻结预训练评论家作为部署性能代理，仅在线更新演员。提出TEMPO，用评论家预测分布熵正则与基于分数的难样本记忆及重要性采样稳定更新。在Go1、Go2、G1多种偏移下取得最高80%提升，并在实体Go2负载场景验证有效。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement-learning policies for robot locomotion can fail at deployment when operating conditions shift (e.g., rough or slippery terrain, payload changes, sensing degradation), and retraining or manual recalibration is often infeasible under on-device latency and memory constraints. We study test-time adaptation (TTA) for robotic control: adapting a pretrained policy online and in a self-supervised manner during execution, without access to rewards. Our starting point is a lightweight baseline that updates only the actor using a frozen pretrained critic as a deployment-time performance surrogate. Building on this, we introduce TEMPO, a test-time entropy-regularized, memory-guided policy optimization method that stabilizes critic-driven updates under severe shift. TEMPO combines (i) an entropy-promoting regularizer on the critic's predictive distribution to mitigate overconfident extrapolation, and (ii) a score-based memory, inspired by prioritized replay, that prioritizes low-value ("hard") observations and applies importance sampling to focus limited computation on the most informative deployment conditions. Across Go1, Go2, and G1 in MuJoCo Playground under four representative shifts and multiple architectures, TEMPO yields consistent gains, reaching up to 80% improvement in a single-device setting. We further validate on a physical Unitree Go2 with an added calf payload, where fully on-device adaptation improves performance over the non-adapted baseline across real-world episodes.

papers.title_en: Learning Structured Locomotion References for Optimization-Based Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Ömer Tarık Banuş, Uluç Saranlı, M. Mert Ankaralı
papers.evidence: 分层强化学习结合模型式全身控制用于足式运动
papers.tldr: 四足运动需协调身体、接触力、落脚与步态时序，纯学习或纯模型控制各有局限。本文提出分层控制器：强化学习调节结构化运动参考，步态调度、反应式落脚规划与全身冲量控制器负责高频执行。在六方向扰动课程中训练后，扰动网格平均存活率达77.29%，高于模型参考控制器的50.35%；消融显示自适应落脚贡献最大。结果表明该架构能把学习适应与优化式全身控制有效结合。
papers.abstract_en: Quadruped locomotion requires coordinating body motion,contact forces, foothold placement, and gait timing. We present a hierarchical controller in which reinforcement learning adapts these structured locomotion references while a gait scheduler, reactive footstep planner, and whole-body impulse controller retain responsibility for high-frequency execution. The model-based backbone can sustain a nominal trot independently, allowing the policy to focus on when and how to modify an already functional locomotion controller. We train the complete hierarchy in a vectorized controller-in-the-loop environment using a six-direction disturbance curriculum. Under a common simulator and evaluation protocol, the proposed controller achieves 77.29% mean survival across the tested disturbance grid, compared with 50.35% for the model-based reference controller. Training-time channel ablations identify adaptive foothold placement as the largest marginal contributor to grid survival and reveal direction-dependent effects of gait-rate adaptation. Together, these results demonstrate the viability of the proposed hierarchical controller architecture for integrating learned adaptation with optimization-based whole-body control through structured locomotion references.

papers.title_en: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
papers.authors: Tianqi Liu, Hanfei Zhao, Qifeng Liang, Hui En Pang, Jiarui Xu, Sayang Mu, Penghao Qiu, YingSheng Zhang, Jun Wang, Ziang Cao, Mingze Sun, Yukang Cao, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Ziwei Liu
papers.evidence: 跨人类与机器人具身的第一视角移动操作世界模型
papers.tldr: 面向跨具身机器人联合建模移动与操作时，动作空间异构且多模态监督稀缺。Ropedia W0 构建含1万小时人类与3千小时机器人自我中心数据的Xp-Data，用统一运动学表示编码相机位姿和投影骨架，并提出Xp-Teleop长时程基准。模型在五个跨具身基准及留出人类视频上取得领先，蒸馏后支持实时分钟级推演与VR交互，展示世界模型在具身决策中的应用潜力。
papers.abstract_en: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, $Ψ_0$, $ω$-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.

papers.title_en: Locomotion with Online Awareness of Dynamics for Precision Footholds
papers.authors: Kunzhao Ren, Zhishuo Zhu, Xiaobin Xiong
papers.evidence: 深度感知行走策略与惯性估计结合用于地形通过
papers.tldr: 未知负载会改变机器人动力学，在狭窄落脚边界上难以精确接触。LOAD将显式惯性估计与隐式动力学特征结合，用循环模块从本体感知推断躯干惯性变化和任务历史，并将高度图教师蒸馏为深度学生策略。仿真与硬件实验显示隐式特征加速训练、显式估计提升成功率，二者结合接近特权策略，并实现单侧负载6 kg通过10 cm横梁、9 kg通过15 cm横梁及均布11 kg通过15 cm横梁。
papers.abstract_en: Unknown payloads alter robot dynamics and make precise contact execution difficult when foothold margins are small. We present LOAD, a perceptive locomotion framework that combines explicit inertial estimates with implicit dynamics features for narrow-beam traversal. Separate recurrent modules infer torso inertial changes and task-relevant history from proprioception, while a height-map teacher is distilled into a depth-based student. We extensively evaluate LOAD and its variants in simulation and on hardware across beam widths and payload configurations. The results show that implicit dynamics features accelerate training, while explicit inertial estimation further improves traversal success; combining both enables LOAD to approach the performance of a privileged policy supplied with ground-truth inertial parameters. Hardware experiments demonstrate traversal with unilateral payloads of 6 kg on a 10 cm beam and 9 kg on a 15 cm beam, and an evenly distributed 11 kg payload on a 15 cm beam. These results support combining physical estimates and history features for precision locomotion under unknown loads.
